fortran.note: ifort is not installed on this host, so gfortran reproduces the -r8/-i4 precision contract only. This is not a claim of ifort-identical code generation. gfortran 16 implements the Fortran 2023 SPLIT intrinsic, which shadows this project's split.f and makes soil.f fail with 'Too many arguments in call to split' even though the call is correct (split.f declares 10 arguments, soil.f passes 10). Declare EXTERNAL split after that unit's header, or compile that one unit with -std=f95.

zig_targeted_tests.known_failure_mode: CORRECTION recorded 2026-09-22 later the same day: the direct `zig test` form ALSO hangs, so it is not a reliable workaround. Observed twice consecutively: both zig processes sat at EXACTLY 0 CPU-seconds delta over 60 s, produced no output, spawned no compiler child, and wrote nothing to the global zig cache for over three hours. Distinguishing a real hang from buffered progress needs three signals together: zero CPU delta over >=60 s, no new writes under %LOCALAPPDATA%\zig, and no build-exe/compile child process. The toolchain itself was proven healthy at the same moment by compiling and running a trivial one-test file in 25.5 s, so this is specific to this test binary and NOT an environment fault. A ReleaseSafe build of the same tree is the available compilation check when this hang occurs; it is weaker than the suite because it does not compile test blocks.
